cls: Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (non-glycosylated deletion mutant) - thrombolytic / fibrinolytic
quick: STEMI: 10 units IV bolus, then a second 10-unit IV bolus 30 minutes later (double-bolus)
Not applicable - IV use only in an acute care setting
Use only if the potential benefit justifies the risk; thrombolysis carries maternal/fetal bleeding risk
Caution; no data - consider interrupting breastfeeding briefly
No specific dose adjustment; bleeding risk higher in liver disease
Not relevant to acute single-use administration
Signs of bleeding (especially intracranial), neurologic status, ECG, blood pressure, hemoglobin
summary: Reteplase is a recombinant non-glycosylated deletion mutant of human tissue plasminogen activator used to dissolve coronary thrombi in acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction. It is given as a fixed double-bolus and works by converting plasminogen to plasmin, lysing fibrin. Its principal danger is bleeding, including intracranial hemorrhage and stroke.
indications: Management of acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) in adults, to improve ventricular function, reduce the incidence of heart failure, and reduce mortality

dosage.d: 10 units IV bolus over 2 minutes, then a second 10 units IV bolus 30 minutes later
dosage.n: Each bolus over ~2 min; flush line before and after with saline

dosage.d: Use with aspirin and heparin per protocol
dosage.n: Do not mix reteplase with other medications in the same line

admin: Reconstitute only with the supplied sterile water; give as an IV bolus over about 2 minutes
Do not give heparin and reteplase through the same IV line without flushing with saline first
Administer the second 10-unit bolus 30 minutes after the first
Initiate as early as possible after symptom onset
Have resuscitation and bleeding-control measures available
moa: Reteplase is a recombinant plasminogen activator that catalyzes the cleavage of endogenous plasminogen to plasmin. Plasmin degrades the fibrin matrix of the thrombus, producing clot lysis and reperfusion. It is a deletion mutant of native tPA with reduced fibrin binding, giving a longer half-life that allows fixed bolus dosing.

absolute: History of cerebrovascular accident / any prior hemorrhagic stroke or stroke within recent period
Recent intracranial or intraspinal surgery or trauma
Intracranial neoplasm, arteriovenous malformation, or aneurysm
relative: Recent major surgery or trauma (within ~10 days)
Acute pericarditis, subacute bacterial endocarditis, diabetic hemorrhagic retinopathy

preg: There are no adequate human data. Thrombolytics carry a significant risk of maternal hemorrhage (and potential placental/fetal bleeding). Use only if the potential benefit clearly justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether reteplase is excreted in human milk. Given the brief use and rapid clearance, a short interruption of breastfeeding may be considered; use caution.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment has been established for renal impairment.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is defined, but bleeding risk is increased in significant hepatic disease (coagulopathy); use with caution.

major: Antiplatelet agents (aspirin, clopidogrel, GP IIb/IIIa inhibitors) - increased bleeding
interactions.diagnostics: Coagulation tests (fibrinogen, fibrin degradation products) are altered; reteplase may interfere with thrombin-time and fibrinogen assays

monitoring: Continuous monitoring for bleeding, especially neurologic signs of intracranial hemorrhage
counsel: This clot-dissolving medicine is given in hospital during a heart attack
It can cause bleeding - report any unusual bruising, blood in urine/stool, or severe headache immediately
Avoid unnecessary needle sticks and injury during and after treatment
Tell the team about all blood thinners and any recent surgery, injury, or stroke
pk: Clot lysis begins within minutes of administration
Rapid fibrinolytic effect after each bolus
Store the kit at 2-25 C; reconstitute immediately before use and use promptly
pearls: Given as a simple fixed double-bolus (10 + 10 units, 30 min apart) - no weight-based calculation, unlike alteplase
Primary danger is bleeding, above all intracranial hemorrhage - screen contraindications carefully
Earlier administration after symptom onset gives greater myocardial salvage
NOTE: reteplase (Retavase) is FDA-approved as a biologic (BLA) and is therefore not in the openFDA drug-label dataset; content here follows the approved Retavase prescribing information
missed: Not applicable - reteplase is an emergency single-course thrombolytic given by clinicians, not a self-administered maintenance medication.
overdose: Overdose increases the risk of serious bleeding. There is no specific reversal agent; management is to stop the drug and any concomitant heparin/antiplatelet therapy, apply local pressure, and give supportive care including transfusion of blood products (packed cells, fresh frozen plasma, cryoprecipitate, platelets) and antifibrinolytics (e.g., tranexamic acid/aminocaproic acid) as needed.
